highlights.title: Causal adaptive OSD retains the terminal-distance residual
highlights.plain: Orabona, Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization, arXiv:1912.13213v10 (2026-06-21), printed13-14/PDF25-26 and printed39-40/PDF51-52; SHA256 cef4edfa97a6e063e53e9c532717c50aa156e5bc782ea49f969b3385011a1b17. For the actual causal projected trajectory with eta_t=alpha*D/sqrt(S_(t+1)) and zero-feedback skipping, the regret is bounded by (1/(2alpha)+alpha)*D*sqrt(S_T) minus the terminal squared distance times sqrt(S_T)/(2alpha D). The reusable potential theorem separately permits signed real a_t bounded above by C only at played indices, nonnegative nondecreasing weights and T>0; no terminal bound or lower bound on a_t is added.
highlights.intuition: For D>0, legal supporting planes and projection nonexpansiveness give the one-step distance and energy estimate. Summation by parts controls the distance terms with monotone weights sqrt(S_(t+1))/(2alpha D), retaining the signed terminal term. The shared adaptive-energy sum controls the feedback terms. Empty horizons vanish; D=0 forces feasible played and comparator points to coincide, so it is proved separately without dividing by D. Totalized real division makes the displayed residual zero at D=0. Quantitatively, writing a_t=||x_t-u||^2 and delta_t=ell_t(x_t)-ell_t(u), the D>0 one-step result is delta_t <= (a_t-a_(t+1))*sqrt(S_(t+1))/(2alphaD) + (alphaD/2)*||g_t||^2/sqrt(S_(t+1)). The shared energy theorem gives sum(t<T)||g_t||^2/sqrt(S_(t+1)) <= 2sqrt(S_T), so its scaled contribution is at most alphaD sqrt(S_T). If an inclusive energy is zero, nonnegativity forces the current support to be zero; the totalized 0/0 summand is zero and the actual algorithm skips. No positive-energy premise is added.

highlights.intuition: Set alpha=sqrt(2)/2 in the general theorem and simplify its coefficient to sqrt(2), then discard the nonnegative residual. Independently reuse the shared optimal-step lower bound and positive argmin for the scalar benchmark. In each one-zero case construct arbitrarily small positive upper-bound values; the existing strict-decrease facts rule out attainment.
